findings.summary: At server concurrency eight, NACA OCR takes 81.6% of the measured call. Queues are smaller but still reach four waiting requests per GPU.
observations: Median full call: 3.28 s; OCR 2.68 s; embedding 0.46 s. One warm-up and three ordinary measurements are separate from the instrumented call.
Each server reached eight running requests. Waiting queues peaked at four and were nonempty in 18–24% of measured OCR-window samples (76–77 request samples per GPU).
GPU-busy means during OCR were 85.4%, 86.0%, 97.4% and 83.9% across GPUs 0–3; seven or eight one-second samples per GPU. These are activity measurements, not peak-compute percentages.
The complete instrumented output passed the original frozen reference. The five-PDF evaluator independently passed all thirty calls for this configuration.
Client concurrency remains four per GPU per page worker, with at most four page workers; server concurrency sixteen covers that admission ceiling.
findings.next_step: Test server concurrency sixteen with dynamic pages and the same clients; then reassess the remaining bottleneck.
findings.optimization: Preserve BF16/16-chunk embeddings, window 64, dynamic pages, batch invariance and all frozen OCR settings. Increase only server max_num_seqs.
